description: Fix the user-reported bug: clicking a movie/TV series after APK update returns 'Something went wrong - API Error 404'. Root causes: (1) The Cloudflare Pages function and middleware regex routes only match numeric IDs (\d+), but the mobile 'My List' feature can store items that persist across APK updates and may have stale or non-numeric IDs. (2) More importantly, the TMDB API itself can return 404 for individual movies/shows that have been removed, but the error message is generic and doesn't help the user. (3) The functions file has no /tv/on-the-air, /anime/*, or /discover/* routes, causing 404 for those endpoints when deployed to Cloudflare Pages.
steps: Step 1 - Fix functions/api/[[path]].js: Add missing routes that exist in middleware.js but not in the functions file: /tv/on-the-air, /anime/trending, /anime/ongoing, /anime/top-rated, /discover/movie, /discover/tv. Copy the route handler logic from the middleware.js to the functions file for consistency.

Step 2 - Fix ID regex patterns: In both functions/api/[[path]].js and middleware.js, change the movie/tv detail route regex from (\d+) to ([\w]+) to also handle alphanumeric IDs. This allows IDs like 'tt1234567' (IMDB) to pass through to TMDB - TMDB will return 404 for invalid IDs which we then handle gracefully.

Step 3 - Improve TMDB 404 error handling: In both functions/api/[[path]].js, middleware.js, and apps/server/src/index.js, when fetchTMDB throws with status 404, return a user-friendly 404 response with message 'Content not found' instead of the generic 502 'Bad Gateway'. Update fetchTMDB to distinguish between 404 (content not found) and other errors.

Step 4 - Improve frontend error display: In apps/web/src/utils/api.js (web) and packages/shared/utils/api.js (mobile shared), when the API returns 404, throw a more descriptive error message like 'Content not found or has been removed' instead of the generic 'API Error: 404 Not Found'.
Step 5 - Verify all changes pass lint/typecheck/build/test.
acceptance_criteria: functions/api/[[path]].js has parity with middleware.js for all API routes
Non-numeric IDs in detail routes return 404 with clear message instead of falling to catch-all
TMDB 404 errors return 404 (not 502) with user-friendly message
Frontend shows 'Content not found or has been removed' for 404 responses
All verification commands (lint, typecheck, build, test) pass
findings: All missing routes were already present in functions/api/[[path]].js (likely added in a previous commit). Applied regex fix from (\d+) to ([\w]+) across all 3 API handlers, added err.status propagation in fetchTMDB, added 404-specific catch handling, and improved frontend error messages. All verification commands pass: lint, typecheck, build, and 42 tests.
